page: OVHcloud rtx5000-56 is a GPU-accelerated cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 8 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 56.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per core. For graphics and parallel computing workloads, the instance is equipped with two NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs from the Turing architecture family, delivering a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and the instance is provisioned with 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average performance across standard compute and memory operations. The Intel Xeon W-3235 processor achieves middle-tier results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as in Geekbench single-core and multi-core suites. However, certain bottlenecks are present, particularly in large-block memory write bandwidth and single-threaded gzip compression, both of which fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers. Conversely, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance in Passmark memory testing, placing in the top 25%. Its primary strength lies in GPU-accelerated tasks; LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models show top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the rtx5000-56 offers a balanced resource profile for workloads requiring dedicated GPU acceleration without the premium cost of newer-generation enterprise accelerators. The inclusion of dual Turing-generation GPUs with 32 GB of total VRAM makes this instance highly suitable for machine learning inference on small to medium models, ray tracing, and image processing. However, the average CPU performance and weak large-block memory write speeds suggest it is less optimal for heavy CPU-bound compilation or high-throughput database write operations. It is best deployed for GPU-driven workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, 3D rendering, and data science tasks.
